resumen: Must / have to: obligación en presente: I must finish this today. We have to wear a uniform. Must no tiene pasado; se usa had to: I had to get up at five.
Mustn't / don't have to / needn't: mustn't prohíbe (You mustn't use your phone); don't have to y needn't solo dicen que no hace falta: You don't have to wear a suit.
Consejo: should y ought to + infinitivo (You ought to rest); had better ('d better) es más urgente y va sin to: You'd better not be late. Para criticar el pasado: You should have told me.
Deducción en presente: must be (seguro que sí), might/could be (quizás), can't be (seguro que no): It can't be Marta; she's in Spain.
Deducción en pasado: modal + have + participio: It must have rained. I might have left them at work. He can't have read it. En afirmativa no existe can have.

Habilidad: can/could para la habilidad general; be able to en los tiempos que can no tiene (I won't be able to come). Para un logro concreto en el pasado, managed to o was able to, no could: We managed to catch the train.
Needn't have / didn't need to: I needn't have cooked so much = lo hice y no hacía falta; I didn't need to take a taxi = no hacía falta y, normalmente, no lo hice.
Be supposed to: lo que se espera según una norma o lo que dice la gente: We aren't supposed to eat here. The library is supposed to be amazing.

preguntas.q: You ___ wear a suit to the interview, but you can if you want to.
preguntas.x: Don't have to indica que algo no es obligatorio. Mustn't y can't lo prohibirían, lo que contradice you can if you want to, y don't must no existe.

preguntas.q: You ___ use your phone during the exam, or they'll take your paper away.
preguntas.x: Mustn't expresa prohibición. Don't have to y needn't solo dicen que no es necesario, lo que no encaja con la amenaza, y después de must nunca va to.

preguntas.q: I ___ get up at five yesterday because my flight was at seven.
preguntas.x: Must no tiene pasado; la obligación pasada se expresa con had to: I had to get up. Must y have to no concuerdan con yesterday, y musted no existe.

preguntas.q: You look exhausted. You ___ go to bed earlier.
preguntas.x: Should + infinitivo sin to da un consejo: You should go to bed earlier. Ought sí necesita to (ought to go), pero ni should ni must van seguidos de to.

preguntas.q: You've been travelling for twenty hours! You ___ be really tired.
preguntas.x: Para una deducción casi segura en presente se usa must be. Can't be diría lo contrario, mustn't expresa prohibición y can no sirve para deducir algo concreto.

preguntas.q: Someone's knocking at the door. It ___ Marta; she's on holiday in Spain.
preguntas.x: Para una deducción negativa en presente se usa can't be: estoy seguro de que no es ella. Must be y might be contradicen que está en España, y can't have been se refiere al pasado.

preguntas.q: The streets are all wet. It ___ during the night.
preguntas.x: Una deducción segura sobre el pasado se forma con must have + participio: must have rained. Had to rain expresa obligación, no deducción, y must rain se refiere al presente.

preguntas.q: I'm afraid I won't ___ come to the meeting tomorrow.
preguntas.x: Can no tiene futuro ni infinitivo, así que después de will/won't se usa be able to: won't be able to come. Dos modales no pueden ir juntos (won't can), y able necesita be.

preguntas.q: The traffic was terrible, but we ___ catch the last train.
preguntas.x: Para un logro concreto en el pasado se usa managed to (o were able to); could en afirmativa expresa habilidad general (I could swim at five), no un éxito puntual. Succeed va con in + -ing.

preguntas.q: The last bus leaves at eleven. You ___ hurry or you'll miss it.
preguntas.x: Had better (contraído, 'd better) + infinitivo sin to da un consejo urgente. La contracción 'd es had, no would, y nunca va seguida de to.

preguntas.q: We ___ eat at our desks, but almost everyone does.
preguntas.x: Be supposed to indica lo que se espera por una norma, aunque no se cumpla: We aren't supposed to eat here. Se forma con be + el participio supposed, no con do ni con -ing.

preguntas.q: I failed the exam. I ___ harder last term.
preguntas.x: Para criticar o lamentar algo del pasado se usa should have + participio: should have worked. Must have worked es una deducción («seguro que trabajé más»), que no tiene sentido después de suspender.

preguntas.q: Which sentence is correct?
preguntas.a: I'd love to be able to speak Japanese.
d: I'd love to can speak Japanese.
I'd love to could speak Japanese.
I'd love that I can speak Japanese.
preguntas.x: Can no tiene infinitivo, así que después de to se usa be able to: I'd love to be able to speak. To can y to could no existen, y love that I can es un calco de «me encantaría que pudiera».

preguntas.q: I'm not sure where my keys are. I ___ them at the office, or maybe they're in the car.
preguntas.x: Para una posibilidad en el pasado se usa might have + participio (también may have o could have). Must have es demasiado seguro para or maybe, y can have no se usa en afirmativa.

preguntas.q: Leo ___ the email; he's been offline all week.
preguntas.x: Una deducción negativa sobre el pasado se forma con can't have + participio: es imposible que lo haya leído. Must have read contradice la evidencia, y shouldn't have read critica una acción en lugar de deducir.

preguntas.q: Ana gave me a lift to the station, so I ___ a taxi.
preguntas.x: Didn't need to dice que algo no fue necesario y, normalmente, que no se hizo: no tomé taxi. Needn't have taken significaría que sí lo tomé sin necesidad, lo que contradice que me llevaron.

preguntas.q: Choose the sentence that means the same as: 'I took an umbrella, but it didn't rain, so it wasn't necessary.'
preguntas.a: I needn't have taken an umbrella.
d: I can't have taken an umbrella.
I mustn't have taken an umbrella.
I wouldn't have taken an umbrella.
preguntas.x: Needn't have + participio expresa que hicimos algo que no era necesario: I needn't have taken an umbrella. Can't have taken es una deducción («es imposible que lo llevara»), no una falta de necesidad.

preguntas.q: You ___ told me the meeting was cancelled; I waited for an hour.
preguntas.x: Ought to have + participio, igual que should have, critica algo que no se hizo en el pasado. Ought siempre lleva to, y después va have, no had.

preguntas.q: Which sentence is correct?
preguntas.a: You'd better not tell anyone about this.
d: You'd better don't tell anyone about this.
You'd not better tell anyone about this.
You'd better to not tell anyone about this.
preguntas.x: La negativa de had better se forma con not después de better: You'd better not tell. No se usa don't ni to detrás de better.

preguntas.q: Choose the sentence that means the same as: 'Everyone says the new library is amazing.'
preguntas.a: The new library is supposed to be amazing.
d: The new library supposes to be amazing.
The new library should have been amazing.
The new library must have been amazing.
preguntas.x: Be supposed to be también significa «dicen que es»: It's supposed to be amazing. Should have been indica una expectativa que no se cumplió, y must have been es una deducción sobre el pasado.
